group_assessment.weighting: Retrospective single-centre cohort of 208 admissions (98 adults, mean age about 35 years, mean BMI 12.2, 97% female) with route-specific calorie quantification by nursing meal-consumption scores, mixed-effects regression of nadir phosphorus, potassium, magnesium and calcium. The reported fact is an association of parenteral dextrose calories with magnesium and calcium falls after Bonferroni adjustment, not phosphorus; the mechanism offered is untested and confounding by indication is acknowledged. Adults with a psychiatric illness; no children, no encephalopathy, no WWOX, and the text never mentions thiamine (string search over the rendered text returned 0).

entries.proposition: Retrospective single-centre analysis of 208 admissions of 98 adults with anorexia nervosa treated over 25 years.
entries.snippet: During this period, 208 admissions occurred among 98 patients with anorexia nervosa

entries.proposition: The cohort was severely underweight (mean BMI 12.2).
entries.snippet: The mean BMI across all 208 admissions was 12.2 ± 2.2, indicating that the cohort predominantly comprised individuals with extreme malnutrition

entries.proposition: Mean intake over seven days was 1443 kcal/day, of which 334 kcal/day was parenteral; parenteral nutrition was about 81% carbohydrate.
entries.snippet: carbohydrate proportions were approximately 60%, 54%, and 81% for the regular diet, enteral formulas, and parenteral nutrition, respectively

entries.proposition: The non-oral exposure mixed intravenous fluid therapy, peripheral and total parenteral nutrition and was grouped only by whether it contained dextrose.
entries.snippet: consisted of a mixture of intravenous fluid therapy, peripheral parenteral nutrition, and total parenteral nutrition
entries.anchor: Methods, Assessment of route-specific caloric intake

entries.proposition: Main result: regular diet, enteral formula and non-dextrose parenteral calories were not associated with nadir electrolytes; higher parenteral dextrose intake was associated with lower nadir magnesium and larger percent falls in magnesium and calcium.
entries.snippet: higher parenteral dextrose intake was associated with lower nadir magnesium and greater percent decreases in magnesium and calcium during refeeding (Table 4)

entries.proposition: For phosphorus, the electrolyte most often tied to refeeding syndrome, the dextrose coefficient was not significant for nadir level (p 0.0702) and the percent-decrease p 0.0212 was unadjusted.

Table 4 lists the magnesium nadir coefficient for parenteral dextrose as -0.119; Table 7 for the same model gives -0.0119 with standard error 0.00258 (ten-fold difference; a typographical error in one table is likely, not resolvable from the paper).
Table 7 gives the magnesium nadir coefficient as -0.0119.
Only 9 admissions with predominantly parenteral intake had magnesium data in the subgroup analysis.
entries.snippet: Participants with parenteral intake (n = 18 for P; 18 for K; 9 for Mg; 15 for Ca)

entries.proposition: Nadir analyses excluded admissions without a V-shaped trajectory, mostly early self-discharge.
entries.snippet: trajectory during this period were excluded from

entries.proposition: The authors name confounding by indication: parenteral nutrition may have gone to sicker patients.
entries.snippet: However, parenteral nutrition may have been preferentially administered to more severely ill patients, and residual confounding by indication cannot be entirely excluded.

entries.proposition: Parenteral nutrition was not stratified by continuous versus intermittent infusion, which may change insulin surges.
entries.snippet: which may influence the magnitude of insulin surges during refeeding

entries.proposition: The route-specific mechanism the authors favour (hepatic first-pass buffering) was not measured.
entries.snippet: glucose handling were not directly evaluated in this study

entries.proposition: The authors suggest parenteral nutrition with more lipid and less carbohydrate might have been preferable.
entries.snippet: a greater use of lipids in parenteral nutrition might have been preferable

entries.proposition: Figure 1 shows 208 admissions: 203 fed orally, 142 with parenteral nutrition, 137 combined oral and parenteral, and only 5 exclusively parenteral.
